blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning, Explained: Why Rotating Neurons Beats Low‑Rank Tweaks
blogs.description: A beginner-friendly tour of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): how orthogonal transformations preserve pairwise neuron angles and spectral norms, why that helps generalization and stability, and how OFT compares to LoRA, adapters, and prompt tuning. We’ll also unpack why OFT’s original block‑diagonal design saves parameters but hurts expressiveness.

blogs.title: From Wi‑Fi to Weights: An Information‑Transmission View of Finetuning
blogs.description: The paper’s key mental model, without the math. We reimagine dense matrix construction as routing signals through a grid network: edges become non‑zeros, paths become factorized matrices. You’ll learn the two big design goals—dense connectivity and minimal free edges—and how this perspective leads to smarter, sparser parameterizations.

blogs.title: Meet BOFT: Butterfly Orthogonal Finetuning That Shrinks d² to d log d
blogs.description: An accessible deep dive into BOFT, the paper’s new method that factorizes an orthogonal matrix into butterfly components inspired by the Fast Fourier Transform. We’ll explain the m and b knobs, how BOFT builds dense rotations from sparse pieces, identity initialization, multiplicative dropout, and why there’s zero added inference latency after merging.

blogs.title: Hands‑On BOFT: How to Apply Butterfly Finetuning to LLMs, Vision, and Diffusion
blogs.description: A practical guide to using BOFT in real models: where to insert it, how to pick m and b under a parameter budget, initialization and regularization tips, and what to expect in training time vs memory footprint. We’ll cover integration patterns for language models, vision transformers, and text‑to‑image diffusion models.

blogs.title: Expressivity vs Regularity: Why Structured Rotations Generalize Better
blogs.description: We explore why BOFT can be more expressive than block‑diagonal OFT at the same parameter cost, how butterfly structures can approximate classic transforms, and the kaleidoscope hierarchy for dialing expressivity up or down. We’ll also discuss spectral‑norm preservation and the inductive biases that help guard against overfitting.

blogs.title: Results Roundup: BOFT vs SOTA on Language, Vision, and Generative Tasks
blogs.description: A readable summary of the experimental findings. We synthesize how BOFT adapts large vision transformers, LLMs, and diffusion models, the stability and generalization gains observed, and how it compares to strong PEFT baselines. We also call out the main caveat: slightly higher training runtime due to multiple factors, with no inference‑time cost.

blogs.title: What’s Next for Parameter‑Efficient Orthogonal Tuning?
blogs.description: A forward‑looking piece on limitations and opportunities: reducing BOFT’s training overhead, exploring alternative network topologies via the information‑transmission lens, combining BOFT with other PEFT strategies, and hardware‑aware implementations. We outline open questions the paper raises for the community.
